facts.text: In S1_R05/P7 ('clean some butterknife and put it in drawer'), drawer 1 contained knife 1 and spatula 1; the Parent took knife 1, cleaned it at the sinkbasin, moved knife 1 to drawer 1, then kept opening drawers/cabinets until step_limit at step 50.

In S1_R05/Q7 (same task), drawer 1 held knife 1 and spatula 1 and drawer 2 was empty; the Candidate cycled drawers 1-6, cabinet 1, and countertops 1-3, whose visible contents (bread, egg, lettuce, mug, plate 3, pot, kettle, ladle, soapbottle, spatula, spoon) include no butterknife; it ended step_limit at step 50.

M10 (based on S1_R05/diff) states that in this clean-butterknife pair no exact butterknife was present, both runs hit the step limit, and the Candidate still cycled among drawers, countertops and cabinets.

answers.conditions: Non-desklamp clean-and-place task requiring an exact target category; each side is a single run under S1_R05/diff; only partial detail windows are supplied.
answers.comparison: The Parent substituted a near-category knife (took, cleaned, placed knife 1); the Candidate refused substitution and kept searching, but its sweep returned to already-open empty drawers/cabinets/countertops instead of new candidates. Neither reached a butterknife.
answers.conclusion: Both executions failed (step_limit, success=false); the only recorded near-match was knife 1, and the Parent's cleaned knife did not satisfy the exact butterknife requirement. The revised sweep did not prevent cycling or rescue this pair, consistent with M10's claim that its rescues depended on the exact target sitting in an uninspected family.
answers.uncertainty: Global absence of a butterknife is not established: many cabinets/countertops were never inspected within the windows shown, and each side ran once, so any claim about unavailable targets or rule causation remains provisional.

facts.text: In S1_R04/P2 ('heat some plate and put it in cabinet'), the Parent reached countertop 3, took plate 3, carried it to the microwave, opened/moved/closing and reopening, took plate 3 back out, heated it, then moved plate 3 to cabinet 1; success in 13 steps.

In S1_R04/Q2 (same task), the Candidate cycled among countertops 1-2, cabinets 1-6 and drawer 1, opening cabinets 2-6 and drawer 1; it never took a plate, never heated anything, and hit step_limit at step 50 while arriving at cabinet 2.

S1_R04/diff added temperature-conditioned placement guidance (heat/cool the held exact target directly, no insertion or door toggling); M7 records that this plate pair failed because the Candidate never reached the countertop where the plate was.

answers.conditions: Non-desklamp heat-and-place task; Parent ran under the pre-edit procedure, Candidate under S1_R04/diff; one run per side, partial detail windows.
answers.comparison: The Parent acquired plate 3 at countertop 3 and performed the full insert/close/reopen/take-out/heat/place sequence (13 steps, success). The Candidate never located or acquired a plate, never applied any temperature action, and spent its 50 steps revisiting cabinets/countertops/drawer 1 (failure).
answers.conclusion: The comparison supports M7's conditional reading: the added heat/cool guidance produced no observable effect here because it operates only after the exact target is acquired; the outcome difference is attributable to search, not to conditioning behavior.
answers.uncertainty: It is unknown whether the Candidate would have performed direct held-target heating had it reached countertop 3, since that state was never observed; single runs and an unobserved plate location limit causal attribution.

facts.text: Current Parent P2 (val:0012, 'put a cool tomato in microwave') first traversed countertop 1, cabinet 1, the fridge and the toaster without finding a tomato, then reached countertop 2 and took tomato 1 at step 13.
Current Candidate Q2 went countertop 1, countertop 2, took tomato 1 at step 5, and performed cool tomato 1 with fridge 1 while holding it at step 7.

Both sides cooled the held tomato with the fridge in a single action (P2:15, Q2:7), then went to the microwave, opened it, and moved the tomato in (P2:16-18, Q2:8-10); both succeeded, in 18 and 10 steps.

The actual edit (u1/u2) expands the search sweep to new candidates and directs conditioning on the held target without door toggling; it preserves exact-category acquisition, direct cooling and placement.

answers.conditions: Same task and initial room; paired whole-task runs (P2/Q2) under the pre-edit and edited skill; one run per side, fixed seed.
answers.comparison: Search/acquisition differed: P2 spent steps 3-13 cycling among fridge, countertop 1 and cabinet 1 before countertop 2, while Q2 reached countertop 2 in 4 steps and acquired the tomato at step 5. Conditioning (one held cool action at the open fridge) and placement (navigate, open microwave, move) are structurally identical; no insertion or door toggling occurred on either side.
answers.conclusion: Both preserved exact-target acquisition, direct cooling, and microwave placement, with identical conditioning/placement structure; the 18-vs-10 step gap is concentrated in search, consistent with the u1 sweep change, while observed behavior already matched the u2 prescription.
answers.uncertainty: Single paired runs cannot isolate rule causation from stochastic variation, and retrieval of the tomato location shows only that Path A cycled more; no unobserved locations or hidden state are available to confirm the step difference is rule-attributable.
